summary.title: Microarchitecture optimizations for exploiting memory-level parallelism
summary.one_liner: Memory-level parallelism (MLP) is the number of cache misses a processor window overlaps, and this paper examines the microarchitecture limits that cap it.
takeaways: Memory-level parallelism is defined as the cache misses that one instruction window overlaps.
ILP techniques such as pipelining, VLIW, superscalar issue, and speculation are the background for this work.
Core microarchitecture limits can cap how much memory-level parallelism a processor achieves.
summary.summary: The page text available is only the Introduction section, so the full technical content is not visible here. It sets the context by describing two decades of ILP research, including pipelining, VLIW, superscalar issue, branch prediction, and data speculation. The listing adds that the paper defines memory-level parallelism as the misses one window overlaps and identifies core limits that cap it. The methods and results beyond the introduction could not be verified from this text.
